identity: A page from the UAE children's magazine مجلة ماجد, from its recurring young-correspondents feature مندوبو ماجد في كل مكان. It is magazine furniture plus an interview, not running prose: page title (مندوبو ماجد في كل مكان), article title (كشافة مجلس التعاون), a correspondent byline (country + town + personal name: سلطنة عمان بهلاء عبد الله بن خليفة الهنائي), a two-sentence news paragraph about the fourth Gulf scout camp at Salalah, a first-person testimonial, two photo captions, a second correspondent byline (اليمن حضرموت حسين صالح باشماخ), a thank-you preamble, and then a seven-question press interview with the UAE ambassador to Yemen, question and answer alternating. Register is simple journalistic Arabic aimed at children.
law: Decisive structural fact: in this document <NL> tracks the PRINTED LINE, not the paragraph. Proof — the page title and the article title get separate <NL>s, every photo caption gets one, and question 7 is split across two <NL> blocks (ما رأيك بمجلة ماجد / وهل من كلمة تريد أن توجهها) even though it is one question. So the layout has already delimited almost every unit for me and the free boundaries are dense. Consequence: inside a <NL> block the natural unit is one finite predication, and I cut only where a conjunct carries its OWN subject or its own full predication (doctrine §0 conjunct-weight test, A1/B3/F4), or where an asyndetic clause introduces a NEW subject (A6). I do NOT cut where the conjunct is a bare noun/adjective in a list (والأمانة والحكمة, والثقافية والسياسية, ودولة الإمارات, وغير المقيم inside بين X وY), where it is a subject-sharing modifier of five words or fewer (short-tail rule 0b), or where it is gapped on the previous verb. Headings, captions and bylines are each exactly one unit: a byline is one credit (place-label + name), on the M1 precedent that سيناريو محمد قنديل is a single unit with no cut between role and name.
reasoning: Seven internal cuts, and the non-cuts matter as much. (1) @31 صلالة: asyndetic, but أبدى قائد المخيم brings a genuinely new subject after شاركت وفود…; my asyndeton discriminator (cut when a new subject/topic enters, merge when the same subject keeps being predicated of) fires for CUT, and this is doctrine A6. Tail is 6 words, clear of the short-tail brake. HIGH. (2) @45 المخيم, before حيث: doctrine A3 and G1 record حيث=CUT four times across two genres with no logged exception, and the connective table lists it as an unbraked default CUT. Head 7 words, tail 8 words, so 0b does not apply. I flag honestly that in this journalistic register حيث would plausibly have carried a comma rather than a period; I take the cut because my doctrine is 4-for-4 and my calibration error is 7:1 in the merge direction. MED. (3) @96 ماجد, before وقد أجاب مشكورا: doctrine F4 makes وقد a CUT; the head runs 22 words, far past the two-clause budget (0c), and the subject shifts from the correspondent (أتقدم) to the ambassador (أجاب). Tail is 6 words. HIGH. (4) @179 البلد: the cleanest site in the document — [السفير المقيم هو الذي يقيم في نفس البلد] و[وغير المقيم هو الذي يتردد حسب الضرورة] is exact B2 parallelism, each half with its own subject, its own copula هو and its own finite verb inside its own relative clause. Parallelism defeats the short-tail rule even at 7 words. HIGH. (5) @227 المجالات, before ونحن بدورنا نقوم: maximum conjunct weight — و plus an EXPLICIT subject pronoun نحن, an adverbial بدورنا, a finite verb نقوم, an object and a relative clause, 15 words, with a topic shift from a state of affairs (الارتباط وثيق) to an action by the speaker's side. A1/C1/G3. HIGH. (6) @261 العربي, before وهي مجلة قيمة ومفيدة: و plus its own subject pronoun هي, a fresh nominal predicate and an 11-word لما-complement; compare F3 where فهي تعلم بداخلها and فهو ذو شعر ذهبي both cut. MED, because it is an elaboration of the same topic rather than a new one. (7) @272 والكبار, before وأتمنى: و plus a first-person finite verb, a switch of subject from the magazine to the speaker and a switch of speech act from description to wish. HIGH. NON-CUTS I had to argue against my own under-segmentation bias. (a) Inside السفارة هي رابط بين دولتين تعمل على تطوير العلاقات بينهما: تعمل is asyndetic and finite, which looks like A6, but its subject is the same رابط/السفارة, the fragment is exactly 5 words, and the head is only 5 words — 0b absorbs it, and the whole answer is a 10-word definition. (b) Inside الرجل الدبلوماسي هو الذي تتوفر فيه صفات الصدق والأمانة والحكمة وقادر على تحمل المسئولية المفوضة إليه من قبل الدولة: وقادر is heavy (9 words of complement) and the conjunct-weight test does list participles, but قادر has NO subject of its own — it is a second خبر of the same مبتدأ, and it reads as a fourth item continuing the quality list الصدق والأمانة والحكمة. This is precisely the contrast with @179, where the conjunct DOES supply its own subject; that contrast is what convinces me. (c) Inside القنصلية تختص بشئون رعاياها في الدولة وما يتعلق بشئون التأشيرات وغيرها: وما يتعلق is a free relative, i.e. a nominal complement governed by the same verb تختص, 5 words, so bare-conjunct plus 0b. (d) At @279, before وللقائمين عليها والعاملين التوفيق والنجاح: 5 words, and it is GAPPED on أتمنى (recipient + wished-thing with the verb elided). Gapping coordination cannot cross a sentence boundary, the shape is not parallel to the verb-initial وأتمنى clause so B2 does not fire, and doctrine H4 records the analogous document-final well-wishing formula والله الموفق being absorbed. My least confident non-cut. (e) Both bylines kept whole: سلطنة عمان بهلاء عبد الله بن خليفة الهنائي and اليمن حضرموت حسين صالح باشماخ. Each sits inside a single <NL> block, and since <NL> = printed line in this document each was one printed line; M1 shows role-label + name (سيناريو محمد قنديل) is a single unit, and J4 says cells of one row merge. (f) No cut inside any question: التي and الذي are tight subordinators, and every و in the questions coordinates bare nouns or adjectives.
